title: Edge degradation triage — AWQ/GPTQ/INT8 interplay
content:
Context and summary:

- What happened: After last week’s rollout of AWQ int8 kernels to the edge pool (canary -> region-edge-1), we started getting customer reports of output degradation on some short/structured prompts (few-shot lists, code completion snippets). The degradation manifests as content skew (repeated tokens), occasional hallucinated list items, and a small but measurable drop in pass@1 for our internal code evals.

- Scope: ~0.6% of requests in region-edge-1, concentrated on small-context (<128 token) requests with deterministic templates. Largely observed on medium-sized models (7B-13B). Not a global issue but repeated enough to warrant triage.

- Quick metric snapshot (baseline vs post-rollout):
  - internal-code-eval pass@1 (selected set of 250 snippets): baseline 78.4% -> post-rollout 74.9% (delta -3.5pp)
  - avg tokens per request in affected cohort: 18
  - response P50 latency: 38ms -> 41ms (+3ms)
  - response P95 latency: 120ms -> 152ms (+32ms)
  - error-rate (model exceptions): unchanged

Initial hypotheses (brain dump):

1) numeric precision edge case in AWQ int8 kernel: AWQ’s per-channel scaling introduces small distribution shifts for short contexts leading to different logits early in generation.
2) kernel mismatch path: routing falls back between GPTQ-quantized-variant and AWQ kernel for different layers (mixed-kernel execution) causing kv-cache layout mismatches and additional copies/latency; when the kv-cache is reassembled it loses alignment and the runtime injects padding that changes attention masks for early tokens.
3) micro-batching / batching windows: small requests get batched into mixed precision batches (some items executed on AWQ, some on GPTQ kernels) and the batching scheduler’s BSR (batch shape routing) uses memory coalescing heuristics that cause non-deterministic ordering, exposing non-deterministic kernels.
4) calibration dataset mismatch: AWQ calibration used a different small dataset than production patterns (e.g., missing punctuation-heavy short prompts), leading to poor quant scale coverage for tokens common in code templates.

What we’ve checked so far (evidence):

- Repro on bench node: We recreated affected requests on a local edge hw node (A100-sim config) using the exact model binary that rolled out. Deterministic seed runs show different top-1 token in ~2.8% of runs vs baseline non-quant kernel. Diffing activations at layer outputs shows small but systematic bias in a subset of head outputs in layers 2–6.

- Profiling (nvprof/perf + runtime traces):
  - Observed ~18% higher memcpy activity for short requests post-rollout.
  - Timeline shows kernel-shift events: kernel_awq_layerX -> kernel_gptq_layerY for same request; these switch events coincide with an extra CUDA stream sync and an extra memcpy of ~40–60KB (not huge but happens per-token for early tokens).
  - CPU-side scheduler logs show fallback to gptq variant when a specific per-layer quant flag is unset. There is a conditional in the runtime that chooses kernel variant based on per-layer metadata; metadata mismatch between model package and runtime metadata likely triggers mixed execution.

- Calibration artifacts: AWQ calibration uploads show we used a sample that is biased towards long natural-language paragraphs. Audit of the calibration set used for edge packaging confirms a shortage of short, punctuation-rich sequences.

- Quality metrics by layer: Per-layer KL divergence between baseline FP16 and AWQ-int8 shows spikes in early layers (1–8) for a small set of head indices. GPTQ-int8 runs show a different pattern (more spread but lower peak).

Root-cause candidate (working):

Primary: mixed-kernel execution due to metadata mismatch in the packaged model + insufficient calibration coverage for short/punctuated sequences. The mixed execution path causes the runtime to perform per-layer layout conversions/extra copies which both: 1) slightly change kv-cache memory layout/per-token attention mask offsets (affecting early token logits), and 2) increase tail latency (P95 up).

Secondary: AWQ’s per-channel asymmetric scaling exacerbates small-token distribution differences that are not covered in the calibration set, leading to shifted logits in corner cases.

Planned experiments (short timeline: 1–10 days):

A) Deterministic single-run experiments\   - Repackage the model with correct per-layer metadata (force homogenous kernel selection: AWQ-only; GPTQ-only) and re-run the 250-snippet eval. Purpose: confirm mixed-kernel hypothesis.\   - Metrics: pass@1, per-token KL, activation diffs, p50/p95 lat.

B) Calibration stress tests\   - Rebuild AWQ calibration using a focused short-sequence corpus (300k sequences from code templates, bullet lists, system prompts) and re-quantize. Compare logits and eval.\   - Also generate hybrid calibration sets (50/50 long/short) to see sensitivity.

C) Micro-batching scheduler simulation\   - Run scheduler with synthetic traffic matching edge-sample arrival (burstiness, small token sequences) and inspect whether batching coalescer mixes kernel types. Add deterministic counters for kernel variant mixing.

D) Kernel instrumentation\   - Add temporary trace points inside the kernel-selection path to log per-request kernel selection per-layer and emit a unique request id to correlate with profiler traces.

E) A/B mitigation runs\   - Canary rollback of AWQ to region-edge-1 for 24h on 10% traffic (fast rollback path tested). Observe whether metrics return to baseline.\   - Alternative: force AWQ-only path (no mixed kernels) and test quality and perf.

Immediate actions taken (so far):

- Rolled back full-rollout to keepers: we paused further AWQ promotion pending triage (RINF-2147).
- Added detector rule in console for signatory quality drop (auto-alert when pass@1 drops by >2pp in a 1-hour window for canary cohorts).
- PR opened to add a preflight model-package validator that checks per-layer metadata vs runtime expectations (PR: runtime#3142).

Open questions / unknowns:

- Why does mixed kernel selection happen for a small subset of layers only? Is this due to model package corruption or an earlier model conversion script that left deprecated flags?
- Is there quant noise amplification when AWQ and GPTQ kernels are adjacent in the graph? Could a dequant->requant boundary introduce small deterministic rounding differences that cascade?
- Are there hardware-specific differences (edge instance GPU microcode / driver) making memcpy behavior non-deterministic?

Action items and owners (short-term):

- Maya: repackage model with forced single-kernel (AWQ-only and GPTQ-only) and run determinism tests (target: 2027-06-12).
- Ethan: instrument kernel-selector traces and add request-id logging in the canary path (target: 2027-06-13).
- Priya: rebuild AWQ calibration with short-seq corpus and produce quant artifacts (target: 2027-06-15).
- Jorge: run scheduler micro-batching simulation and capture kernel-mix frequency (target: 2027-06-14).
- Samira: monitor production alerting rule and compile customer examples for diagnosis (ongoing).

Longer-term ideas / mitigations:

- Enforce model-package signed metadata and add CI gating to prevent mismatched packages from entering canary pools.
- Per-layer selective quantization policy: allow us to opt layers 1..K to use fp16/fp32 while others use AWQ-int8 to avoid early-layer distribution issues.
- Post-quant bias correction: small learned bias vectors applied to final logits to correct systematic shifts introduced by quantization for specific prompt classes.
- Improved calibration: maintain separate calibration profiles per workload class (chat, code, short prompts, bullet lists).

Notes to self / loose ends:

- Save microtrace for request id 20270610-req-0783 (it shows a clean example).
- Check edge packaging pipeline version used for last rollout: pipeline v2.1.4 -> suspect conversion script updated 2027-05-28.
- Cross-check with SRE whether any driver updates were rolled 2027-06-07 in region-edge-1.
